course_info.trial_description:
Exploring English Together: Setting the Foundation for Growth
Hello, I'm Iniobong, an experienced English tutor with 5 years of teaching students at all levels. In my lessons, we will start by identifying your unique goals and developing a personalized learning plan.
I adapt my teaching to suit each student’s needs. Here’s how I approach different areas:
~IELTS/AP English Preparation: Together, we’ll work on your target scores, focusing on the sections you find most challenging.
~Business English: We will focus on effective workplace communication, including presentations, negotiations, and professional email writing.
~Conversational English: Our lessons will concentrate on improving fluency, pronunciation, and boosting your confidence in real-life conversations.
~General English: I’ll design lessons tailored to your personal interests and objectives, helping you develop all four language skills.
The main areas of focus are:
~Exam Preparation: We will practice exam-style questions, refine your strategies, and tackle any weak points.
~Conversational Skills: You’ll participate in discussions, role-plays, and vocabulary-building activities.
~Business English: I’ll create lessons on presentations, meetings, and relevant industry terms.
~General English: We’ll work on listening, speaking, reading, and writing through engaging, hands-on exercises.
My Teaching Approach:
~Communicative Approach: I prioritize student interaction, real-world scenarios, and active participation.
~Task-Based Learning: I’ll assign practical tasks like writing emails or preparing speeches to improve your skills.
~Interactive Learning: Expect to engage in fun activities like games, role-plays, and multimedia tools.
Materials Used:
~Textbooks (for exam prep): Cambridge IELTS, AP English guides, and Business English workbooks.
~Practical Resources: Articles, videos, podcasts, and examples from real life.
~Custom Worksheets: Exercises tailored to your goals.

pro_course_detail.title: Basic English for survival and everyday communication
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Understanding and using common expressions and basic phrases.
Introducing oneself and others, asking and answering simple personal questions.
Basic reading and writing, such as filling out forms or writing short sentences.

Activities:
Vocabulary building: days, numbers, greetings, and common objects.
Role-plays for simple interactions like shopping or asking for directions.
Listening exercises with slow, clear audio for recognition of basic words and phrases.

Grammar:
Present simple tense.
Articles, pronouns, and basic prepositions.

pro_course_detail.title: Expanding communication skills and understanding simple dialogues.
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Communicating in familiar situations, such as ordering food or making appointments.
Reading short texts like advertisements, menus, or basic emails.
Writing simple paragraphs or messages.

Activities:
Vocabulary for common topics: food, family, work, and hobbies.
Listening exercises for identifying details in short conversations.
Speaking drills for basic sentences and short dialogues.

Grammar:
Present continuous and past simple tenses.
Questions (yes/no, WH-questions) and modal verbs (can, must)

pro_course_detail.title: Expanding communication skills and understanding simple dialogues
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Describing events, experiences, and ambitions in detail.
Understanding the main points of clear, standard speech on familiar topics.
Writing connected sentences to form paragraphs.

Activities:
Vocabulary for travel, technology, health, and education.
Role-playing more complex scenarios, such as giving instructions or resolving problems.
Short presentations or discussions on familiar topics.

Grammar:
Future forms (will, going to).
Comparatives, superlatives, and conditional sentences (Type 1)..

pro_course_detail.title: Confidently handling varied language tasks in personal and professional settings.
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Expressing opinions, arguments, and ideas fluently on familiar and some unfamiliar topics.
Understanding the main ideas of complex texts, including technical articles.
Writing detailed essays, reports, and emails.

Activities:
Vocabulary for business, social issues, and culture.
Group discussions or debates on current events.
Listening to interviews, podcasts, or lectures and summarizing them.

Grammar:
Passive voice reported speech.
Conditional sentences (Types 2 and 3), relative clauses.

pro_course_detail.title: Mastery of nuanced and complex language structures.
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Communicating with fluency and spontaneity in diverse situations.
Understanding implicit meanings in both spoken and written texts.
Writing clear, well-structured texts in a range of styles.

Activities:
Vocabulary for academic, technical, and specialized fields.
Writing formal letters, research essays, or professional reports.
Practicing pronunciation and intonation for advanced fluency.

Grammar:
Advanced verb structures (perfect forms, subjunctive mood).
Collocations, idiomatic expressions, and phrasal verbs.

pro_course_detail.title: Near-native proficiency for academic, professional, or personal purposes.
pro_course_detail.description:
Key Skills to be Developed:

Understanding virtually everything heard or read with ease.
Expressing complex ideas fluently and precisely.
Writing sophisticated, nuanced texts like research papers or creative pieces.

Activities:
Analyzing literature, technical documents, and academic works.
Engaging in high-level discussions and presentations.
Practicing advanced writing and editing techniques.

Grammar:
Nuances of tense, mood, and voice.
Refining grammar for stylistic effect and precision.

pro_course_detail.title: Conversational English
pro_course_detail.description:
Welcome to my conversational English lesson! 

This lesson is perfect for students who want to reinforce the knowledge that they already have of English. Here we will focus on improving your natural speech.

So, how is this class any different from the general lessons?

Well, for starters it is less formal. We will use more talking points and dialogue as opposed to exercises. Further, we'll focus more on expanding your vocabulary instead of exposure to grammar structures and new conjunctions through fun, meaningful and exciting conversations. 

 If you have ANY grammar-related questions - or questions related to anything - I am happy to help. This is your time, so feel free to use it as you wish.

For every class, we'll have a topic and focus area, except you have a particular topic in mind, I will  provide at least three topics and you may choose the topic of conversation for the lesson. We'll incorporate idioms, connectors, phrasal verbs, pronunciation techniques and more to improve your conversational English. 

 Also, I give homework for every class.

See you in class!
